approved: Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Information Disclosure, National Interest and Other Measures) Bill 2022
Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development, Communications and the Arts
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change how telecommunications companies share customer information with emergency services and law enforcement.
It would allow the disclosure of unlisted phone numbers and associated details from the Integrated Public Number Database to emergency call persons without consent in certain situations.
The bill would also remove the word 'imminent' from the existing exception for disclosing information to prevent a serious threat to life or health.
Repeals existing provisions that allowed use and disclosure of information from the Integrated Public Number Database for emergency calls.
Inserts a new exception to authorise use and disclosure of unlisted numbers and personal details to emergency call persons when it is unreasonable to obtain consent.
Adds a condition that the person disclosing information must believe it is unreasonable or impracticable to obtain consent.
Removes the 'imminent' qualifier from the exception for disclosing information to prevent a serious threat to life or health.
Telecommunications companies, law enforcement agencies, emergency service organisations, and users of telecommunications services.
Telecommunications Legislation Amendment (Information Disclosure, National Interest and Other Measures) Act 2023
